scenario_description:
Objective: Check the goalball trunk onto the morning Logan flight so the Baltimore qualifier arrival can proceed with required tournament gear.
Emerging Need: The airport bag-drop attempt begins with a posted kiosk payment, then stops when that same station jams before printing a usable tag.
Decision Context: Recovery depends on recognizing that waiting at the failed bay is worse than using stored accessibility-counter instructions and the confirmed assistance request before the bag cutoff.
Consequence: If the recovery path is not used while counter acceptance remains open, the trunk cannot travel on that departure and the tournament plan is disrupted.

parameter.title: Fly to Baltimore for Northeast goalball qualifier
parameter.description: Morning flight with checked goalball trunk required for the qualifier; planned airport arrival 09:00.

parameter.subject: Check-in open for BOS-BWI Flight 1841
parameter.body: Check-in is open for confirmation P7M4QC. Flight 1841 departs Boston Logan Terminal C at 10:15 AM. Customers checking oversized sports equipment should complete bag acceptance before the counter cutoff and keep the bag receipt available at the airport.

parameter.merchant: JetBlue Terminal C Bag-Tag Kiosk C-BAG-03
parameter.description: Checked goalball trunk fee at accessible bag-drop kiosk for BOS-BWI Flight 1841

parameter.content: Status update from Terminal C: Priya has the goalball trunk at accessible bag-drop bay 3. The kiosk accepted the paid reservation, then changed to 'printer jam — attendant override required' before producing a tag. The call button gives no tone, the trunk is still beside her, and the bay line is backing up.

parameter.subject: Bag acceptance closed for BOS-BWI Flight 1841
parameter.body: Baggage acceptance for Flight 1841 closed at 09:35. Unprinted kiosk tags for this departure are void. Please see airport staff about sending checked equipment on a later service.
